messages:
Asha (Finance): Heads up—Finance got two vendor responses for the usage reconciliation tool RFP: PulseBill and MeterLyze. RGTM to do a quick pros/cons and pricing ask here?
Jon (Procurement): Yep—I skimmed both. PulseBill is cheaper on list price, MeterLyze has better line-item parsing for provider-style invoices. Need to confirm overage rules.
Marta (Billing): Important: we need line-level export with normalized token/embedding SKU mapping. Example from AWS-style invoice we get:
```
2025-11-02 | inference.tokens | model-x | 1,234,567 tokens | $0.00040/token
2025-11-02 | embeddings.units | embed-v1 | 3,200 units | $0.0020/unit
```
If vendor can't map these reliably to our internal SKUs, reconciliation is a nightmare.
Victor (Ops): Can MeterLyze handle nested attachments and multipage PDFs? PulseBill says yes in docs but not clear on multi-currency.
ProcureBot: New vendor attachments uploaded: https://redwood.internal/pulsebill-demo & https://redwood.internal/meterlyze-sample-invoices
Asha (Finance): @Jon can you get both to confirm SLA for turnaround on disputed invoices (we typically need 14 days to raise disputes)? Also confirm audit logs and SSO provisioning.
Jon (Procurement): On it. I'm drafting questions: 1) line-item extraction accuracy (sample set), 2) currency conversion handling, 3) dispute SLA and credits, 4) historical export limits, 5) support hours/SLA. Anything else?
Marta (Billing): Add: retention policy for raw parsed data (we need 7 years for some customers) and ability to backfill corrected mappings.
Tess (Legal): Please ask about data residency and contract clause for invoice corrections/credits. Also breach notifications if parsing errors lead to billing mistakes.
Victor (Ops): Also ask about API rate limits for automated pulls—we might pull hourly for several accounts.
Jon (Procurement): Drafting email now, will paste here. PulseBill pricing model: base $1,200/mo + $0.005/line after 100k lines. MeterLyze: base $2,000/mo + $0.003/line, with optional enterprise export add-on ($500/mo). Need usage projection to model cost.
Asha (Finance): Quick estimate: if we process ~10M token-rows/month ~ equivalent 200k lines -> PulseBill marginal ~$500/mo, MeterLyze ~$1000/mo plus add-on. But MeterLyze claims higher accuracy which reduces manual work.
Marta (Billing): Can we get a POC for 30 days with our 3 months of sample invoices? That will let us measure false positives in mapping.
Jon (Procurement): I'll push for POC and a short SOW that includes SLA and credit terms. Will ask both vendors for a one-page mapping doc showing how they map common provider SKUs to our internal taxonomy.
Asha (Finance): Thanks—if MeterLyze will negotiate enterprise export add-on into core for comparable price, I'm leaning toward them despite higher list. Manual reconciliation headcount is expensive.
ProcureBot: Reminder: procurement policy requires 2 quotes >$10k/yr and Security review for vendors with invoice data access.
Tess (Legal): I'll prepare a short exhibit for the invoice-correction clause we can propose.
Jon (Procurement): Email sent to both; I included sample invoices and asked for the mapping doc, POC terms, and dispute SLA. I'll post replies here.
Asha (Finance): Perfect—once replies come in, let's run a quick cost+accuracy tradeoff with estimated FTE savings. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Victor (Ops): If MeterLyze supports SFTP drop and webhook callbacks, that's a win for us.
Marta (Billing): FYI, last time we ran a vendor POC we had to tweak parsing rules for 12 out of 50 provider SKUs. Hoping for better out-of-box coverage this time.
Jon (Procurement): Noted. Will ask for configuration effort estimate.
Asha (Finance): Thanks team—keeping this thread for the vendor replies. :thumbsup:
